scripts.label: Best supported choice
scripts.text: This preserves nearly all that the engine's best move offered. A sound choice can matter without changing the whole game.

scripts.label: Good choice
scripts.text: This keeps most of the position's value, close to the stronger continuations. It is a sound way to carry the game forward.

scripts.label: Human natural error
scripts.text: The human-move model sees this as a natural choice, but the engine finds a stronger move. That contrast is worth studying.

scripts.label: Human hard defense missed
scripts.text: The engine found one move that kept the position playable, and the model evidence suggests it was difficult to find.

scripts.label: Human hard find
scripts.text: The human-move model and the alternatives suggest this was a hard move to find. Keep this idea in mind for similar positions.

scripts.label: Human hard defense found
scripts.text: This move kept the position playable. The human-move model and the searched alternatives suggest it was a hard resource to find.

scripts.label: Human natural best
scripts.text: The human-move model sees this as a natural choice, and it is also the engine's best move.

scripts.label: Human natural strong
scripts.text: The human-move model sees this as a natural choice. It is strong, although the engine prefers another move.

scripts.label: Clock low
scripts.text: The recorded clock shows there was little time left before this move.

scripts.label: Clock fast
scripts.text: The recorded clock shows a quick move with time still available.

scripts.label: Clock long
scripts.text: A substantial amount of recorded time went into this move.

scripts.label: Recognized opening
scripts.text: This is familiar opening territory: the move belongs to a recognized line.

scripts.label: Opening departure
scripts.text: Here the game first steps beyond the line recognized by our opening book.

scripts.label: Recovery assisted
scripts.text: This restores a playable position after the earlier setback. Errors by the other side helped make that recovery possible.

scripts.label: Chance taken
scripts.text: This makes use of the chance the opponent offered on the previous move.

scripts.label: Chance missed
scripts.text: The opponent's previous move offered a chance, but this move lets it pass. Compare the stronger continuation.

scripts.label: Repeated issue
scripts.text: This same issue has appeared before in the reviewed moves of this game. Compare the examples and look for the common warning sign.

scripts.label: Support restored
scripts.text: A piece left unguarded earlier has support again. Compare the two positions to see how its protection changed.

scripts.label: Gradual erosion
scripts.text: This is one of several small concessions that have worsened the position together. Look at the sequence, as well as this move.

scripts.label: Advantage converted
scripts.text: The reviewed moves kept the advantage through to the recorded win. Follow that stretch to see how the advantage was preserved.
